title: The finite smooth trace is the scalar extension of the prime-power trace
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-pur-conventions], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $e\geq1$ be the ramification index, defined by $\ell\mathcal O_E=\varpi_E^e\mathcal O_E$. Let $r\geq1$, put $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$ and $B=\mathcal O_E/\ell^r\mathcal O_E=A_{E,er}$, where the last identification uses $(\ell^r)=(\varpi_E^{er})$. The map $A\to B$ is finite free [lem-coef-finite-free-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the finite constructible finite-Tor categories [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the compact-support functors [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], and the normalized finite smooth traces [def-pur-smooth-trace]. Write $T_A=A_X(d)[2d]$, $T_B=B_X(d)[2d]$ and $t_A:Rf_{!,A}T_A\to A_Y$, $t_B:Rf_{!,B}T_B\to B_Y$ for the unit-coefficient smooth traces. For every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, let
$$c_{B/A,M}:(Rf_{!,A}M)\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,B}(M\otimes_A B)$$
be the finite-free compact-support coefficient map, obtained by extension by zero followed by the proper direct-image tensor comparison, or equivalently by the compact-support projection map for $B$ [def-exchange-projection]. Under the canonical identifications $T_A\otimes_A B\cong T_B$ and $A_Y\otimes_A B\cong B_Y$, one has the equality of morphisms
$$t_B\circ c_{B/A,T_A}=t_A\otimes_A1_B.$$
Thus the normalization of the finite smooth trace over $B$ is exactly the tensor extension of the normalized prime-power trace, including its sign and Tate twist.

proof.text: Write $S_W=-\otimes_A^LB$ and $U_W$ for restriction of scalars, on $W=X,Y$ or a scheme used in a compactification. Specialize [lem-coef-finite-free-extension] to $\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E$, prime-coefficient uniformizer $\ell$ and level $r$. It gives $B=A_{E,er}$ finite free over $A$, with the equality of ideals specified in the statement; no equality of chosen uniformizers is needed. Thus tensoring with $B$ is exact, and all these derived scalar extensions are ordinary tensor extension on complexes. It preserves bounded constructibility: after choosing a finite $A$-basis of $B$, its underlying $A$-complex is a finite sum of copies of the input. Its $B$-Tor interval is the input interval, since for a degree-zero $B$-module sheaf $N$ one has $(M\otimes_A B)\otimes_B^LN=M\otimes_A^LU_WN$. The tensor functors and their canonical reassociations are those of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The construction [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] gives $S_WA_W(d)=B_W(d)$: for the first twist the balancing map is $(z\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto z\otimes ab$ on the common roots-of-unity tower, and then take tensor powers. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] these are rank-one locally free coefficient sheaves, so no higher Tor terms occur, and $T_A,T_B$ are bounded constructible finite-Tor objects. Tensor commutes with the common shift $2d$. Every finite-type $k$-scheme used below is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to the field $k$ (its only ideals are $0,k$). The scalar adjunction $S_W\dashv U_W$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] applied to the identity topos with ring map $A_W\to B_W$. Both functors are exact here: $S_W$ by finite freeness, and $U_W$ because kernels and cokernels have the same underlying abelian sheaves. Their termwise unit $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ and counit $n\otimes b\mapsto bn$ therefore descend through quasi-isomorphisms to derived functors and still satisfy the two triangle identities. This proves the derived adjunction with these actual maps. Restriction also preserves the finite-Tor constructible domain: for a degree-zero $A$-module sheaf $N$, $(U_WK)\otimes_A^LN=U_W(K\otimes_B^L(B\otimes_A N))$, and $B\otimes_A N$ is in degree zero. Constructibility follows by restricting the finite $B$-module stalks on each constructible stratum.

source.place: 2.13: $n=\ell^r$, constant coefficient ring sheaf $B_Y$, and finite-free specialization of the coefficient tensor operation.

proof.text: Fix a compactification $f=pj$ as in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. The open tensor comparison [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] and exactness of $j_!$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] identify $j_!M\otimes_A^LB$ with $j_!(M\otimes_A B)$. These statements also show that $j_!M$ is bounded constructible with the same Tor interval: extend a finite constructible stratification by the closed complement carrying zero, and use the open projection isomorphism to test its Tor bound. Its etale-origin witness exists by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Apply the finite-algebra coefficient comparison [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] to the proper factor $p$ and $j_!M$; it applies to the finite $A$-algebra $B$, not just a quotient of $A$. Compose it with the open coefficient isomorphism to obtain $c_M:S_YRf_{!,A}M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,B}S_XM$. These are actual $B$-linear arrows. For the open coefficient isomorphism use $S\dashv U$ and $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$: the right adjoints of $S_{\bar X}j_!^A$ and $j_!^BS_X$ are identified by $j_A^{-1}U_{\bar X}=U_Xj_B^{-1}$, so their adjoint isomorphism is the stated open tensor map. After restriction of scalars, the proper coefficient map is the counit-defined projection map by [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], and the open map is the open projection map. The restriction/compact-support identification is [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Hence the composite is precisely the specified $c_{B/A,M}$, and its restriction is the compact-support projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection].

source.place: 2.13.1; compactification realization of its tensor comparison. Compare Stacks Tags 0GL5 and 0GL6 (more-etale.tex), projection and change of rings. The finite-free case here is proved by the cited finite-algebra and open comparisons.

proof.text:
For any separated finite-type map $h:V\to W$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes put $P_{h,R}=Rh_{!,R}$ and $G_{h,R}=Rh_R^!$, $R=A,B$. Use the bounded constructible adjunction of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]; the preservation assertion [thm-sf-preservation-class] keeps its exceptional terms in the finite-Tor domain. Define $b_{h,L}:S_VG_{h,A}L\to G_{h,B}S_WL$ to be the $B$-adjoint transpose of
$$P_{h,B}S_VG_{h,A}L\xrightarrow{c_{h,G_{h,A}L}^{-1}}S_WP_{h,A}G_{h,A}L\xrightarrow{S_W\epsilon_{h,A,L}}S_WL.$$
By the adjunction definition, in the $B$-category it satisfies
$$\epsilon_{h,B,S_WL}\,P_{h,B}(b_{h,L})\,c_{h,G_{h,A}L}=S_W(\epsilon_{h,A,L}).\tag{*}$$
Here is a direct proof of invertibility; a general invertible left-adjoint square need not have invertible mate. For arbitrary bounded constructible finite-Tor $K$ on $V$, the scalar adjunction from Step 1, $c$ from Step 2 and the exceptional adjunction give the natural bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,U_VG_{h,B}S_WL)
&=\operatorname{Hom}_B(S_VK,G_{h,B}S_WL)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_B(P_{h,B}S_VK,S_WL)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_B(S_WP_{h,A}K,S_WL)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P_{h,A}K,U_WS_WL)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,G_{h,A}U_WS_WL).
\end{aligned}$$
Thus Yoneda gives an isomorphism $\rho_L:U_VG_{h,B}S_WL\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{h,A}U_WS_WL$. All its objects lie in the tested category by Step 1 and preservation. Choose an $A$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_s$ of $B$. Write $i_{j,H}:H\to U_TS_TH$ for $x\mapsto x\otimes e_j$ on any scheme $T$. The composite $\rho_LU_V(b_{h,L})$ restricts on $i_{j,G_{h,A}L}$ to $G_{h,A}(i_{j,L})$. Indeed, write $i_{j,H}=U(m_{e_j})\eta_H$, with $m_{e_j}$ multiplication by $e_j$ on $S_TH$ and $\eta$ the scalar unit. For the $\eta$ component, the ordinary $A$-adjoint of $\rho_LU(b)\eta$ is $\eta_L\epsilon_{h,A,L}$ by the defining transpose of $b$ and the scalar triangle identities. For $i_j$, the extra multiplication $m_{e_j}$ passes through $c$, $b$ and the $B$-counit because these are $B$-linear, so that adjunct becomes $U(m_{e_j})\eta_L\epsilon_{h,A,L}=i_{j,L}\epsilon_{h,A,L}$. The $A$-adjoint of $G_{h,A}(i_{j,L})$ is the same map by naturality of the exceptional counit. A right adjoint preserves finite products, and finite products and coproducts agree here, so the maps $G_{h,A}(i_{j,L})$ give an isomorphism $(G_{h,A}L)^s\to G_{h,A}(L^s)$. Under the chosen basis this is exactly $\rho_LU_V(b_{h,L})$. Consequently $U_V(b_{h,L})$ is invertible. Finally $U_V$ reflects isomorphisms: a cone with zero restricted cohomology has zero cohomology, since restriction leaves its underlying abelian sheaves unchanged. Hence $b_{h,L}$ is invertible. The basis is used only to prove this fact; the comparison and its counit normalization $(*)$ were defined without it.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.3, counit/transpose normalization. Agent-written finite-free proof of invertibility by scalar/exceptional adjunctions and finite biproducts; no quotient-coefficient exceptional theorem is used.

proof.text: The comparisons just constructed preserve the structural maps used in the diagonal argument, before an orientation is chosen. Here is the map check. An ordinary projection arrow is the adjoint of $(\epsilon^*\otimes1)\mu$, with $\mu$ the tensor/pullback balancing map, by [def-exchange-projection]. Extend this formula to $B$: both orders of the comparison send the tensor factors to the same factors and apply the extended ordinary counit to the first one. The adjunction bijection therefore equates the two $B$-arrows. For the open projection constituent both maps are the same balancing map on the open, and the zero map on the zero extension off it; this identity is termwise and survives sheafification and passage to complexes. For a Cartesian square, the compactification formula of [def-cbc-exchange-map] expresses the proper exchange as a unit/counit mate of the pullback-composition square, and the open exchange is the canonical isomorphism of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]; the two pullback/scalar-extension orders agree by $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab$. Pasting their mates using [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] gives preservation of the compact-support exchange. Its inverse exists on the bounded constructible domain by [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]: the maps are separated finite type, the coefficient rings are finite, and the etale-origin witnesses are supplied as in Step 2. Inverting the commuting comparison square therefore gives preservation of the inverse exchange as well. Finally the dualizing base-change map in [def-pur-co-smoothness] is the adjoint of pulled-back counit after inverse compact-support exchange. Substituting $(*)$ and the preceding exchange identity gives the same $B$-adjoint in either order, so this dualizing base-change map is preserved. The same calculation applies to the tensor map $\theta$: its defining adjoint in [def-pur-co-smoothness] is inverse projection followed by counit tensored with the identity. These computations are equalities of adjoints in the $B$-category; no faithfulness of derived scalar restriction, and no equality test on pro-etale geometric stalks, is used.

proof.text:
Check the orientation at its normalized rank-one model. Let $S$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$, and take the common annihilator $N=\ell^r$. Both coefficient rings are killed by $N$, and $N$ is invertible on $S$. In [def-amb-p1-trace], $h_R$ is the scalar extension of the same $\mathbf Z/N$ Kummer class of $\mathcal O(1)$, and $b_{q,R}$ has components the shifted twisted unit and $h_R$. The balancing identity $(z\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto z\otimes ab$ and the ordinary counit transpose of Step 2 identify $S_Sh_A$ with $h_B$ and identify the first components as well. Consequently, with $c_q$ the proper coefficient comparison and the twists identified,
$$c_qS_S(b_{q,A})=b_{q,B}.$$
Both decompositions are invertible by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], whose finite-ring, invertible-annihilator and Noetherian hypotheses were just checked. Thus the definition $t_{q,R}=\operatorname{pr}_2b_{q,R}^{-1}$ gives the equality
$$t_{q,B}c_q=S_S(t_{q,A})$$
in $D(S_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ by multiplication with the inverses and the unchanged second projection. Restricting along $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$ gives the same equation for affine-line integration: its extra factor is $Rq_*(j_!j^*\to1)$, and the open counit is preserved by the coefficient/open adjunction construction of Step 2. The site comparisons and actual trace-map identities in [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] identify these etale traces, their restrictions, and their adjoint transposes with the ones using the prescribed pro-etale twists. Thus this rank-one calculation fixes the normalization of the maps used here, not only their isomorphism classes.

source.place: 2.13.2 and 3.2.3; explicit normalization check from the projective-line Kummer decomposition. The decomposition and site-map statements cited here fix the otherwise unspecified orientation of the blueprint.

proof.text:
Iterate the rank-one calculation in the ordered coordinate tower of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. At rank zero the trace is the identity and scalar extension preserves it. For rank $m+1$ write $\mathbf A^{m+1}_S\xrightarrow{a}\mathbf A^m_S\xrightarrow{p_m}S$, where $a$ is the final affine-line projection. Its affine-line right adjoint is $G_{a,R}K=a^*K(1)[2]$. The counit at a coefficient $K$ is the open restriction of the formula in [def-amb-p1-trace]: inverse projection followed by $1_K\otimes t_{q,R}$. By Step 4 the projection maps commute with scalar extension; Step 5 gives that equality for $t_q$ and the open counit. Tensoring these equalities with $S K$ therefore proves the affine-line counit equation at $S K$, including when $K=R_{\mathbf A^m}(m)[2m]=G_{p_m,R}R_S$. The inverse projection exists on this bounded finite-Tor input by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]; its twists are locally free by Step 1. The composite counit is precisely $\epsilon_{p_m,R,R_S}\circ P_{p_m,R}(\epsilon_{a,R,G_{p_m,R}R_S})$ by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Substituting the inductive equation and the coefficient-valued affine-line equation proves the scalar equation for the ordered trace of rank $m+1$.
To identify the iterated source with the geometric compact support, use the canonical composition $\alpha_R:P_{p_m,R}P_{a,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{p_ma,R}$ of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Its coefficient equation is
$$c_{p_ma,K}\,S(\alpha_{A,K})=\alpha_{B,SK}\,P_{p_m,B}(c_{a,K})\,c_{p_m,P_{a,A}K}.$$
For this coordinate tower use the product compactifications by projective lines. In their defining proper/open composite, the proper-direct-image constituents obey exactly the composition equation in [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]; the open-extension constituents are the termwise balancing maps of Step 2 and compose by associativity of multiplication in $B$. The intervening proper base-change constituent obeys Step 4's exchange equation. Pasting these three equations gives the displayed equation, with no appeal to faithfulness of restriction. For a proper refinement, the compactification comparison is again a proper-direct-image composite with the open balancing map. Apply the proper composition equation to its proper factor and associativity of the open balancing to its open factor. The resulting commuting refinement square identifies the two coefficient maps. The coherence of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] therefore removes the chosen product compactification. The site comparison in [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] then supplies the pro-etale realization of this ordered trace. All shifts being $2m$ and $2$, their interchange has sign $(-1)^{2m\cdot2}=1$. For a rank-$d$ vector bundle $\pi:V\to S$, [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] characterizes its integration uniquely by these traces on trivializing opens, and [def-amb-vector-integration] states that the gluing is gluing of degree-zero sheaf morphisms. Step 4 permits restriction of the coefficient comparison to each such open. Hence $S_S(t_{\pi,A})c_{\pi,T_A}^{-1}$ restricts to the specified $B$-integration on each open, and that uniqueness gives the global equality with $t_{\pi,B}$. Equivalently, the source is locally isomorphic to the degree-zero unit by the affine-space theorem, and equality of its morphisms to $B_S$ is sheaf-local by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful]. By [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] the inverse vector-bundle dualizing identification of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] is the transpose of this actual integration. Formula $(*)$ and injectivity of the $B$-adjunction Hom bijection therefore show that this particular identification, including its normalization, is preserved by $S$ and $b$. For the etale coordinate localizations used in Step 7, the required total-space localization comparison is also preserved. On ordinary etale sites [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] identifies $u^*G_{h,R}$ with $G_{hu,R}$ for a separated finite-type etale map $u$ into the source of $h$. The identification of the compact support of $u$ with this sum extension, including its actual sum counit, is [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization]; its Noetherian hypotheses follow from Step 1. Thus the localization is the right-adjoint comparison for $P_{h,R}u_!$; $u_!\dashv u^*$ is the exact sum-extension adjunction of that same lemma. Tensoring a sum of sections with $B$ gives the sum of their tensors, so scalar extension commutes with $u_!$, and its counit is the sum of the corresponding sections in both coefficient rings. Pasting this scalar square with that for $P_h$ and taking mates by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] equates the two coefficient/localization orders. For this composition with $u$, use [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. In arbitrary compactifications its construction uses the proper/open interchange of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. The latter statement specifies the sheaf proper/open identification and its derived normalization. The sheaf identification extends a section with its proper support; applying scalar extension sends $x\otimes b$ to that same extended section tensored with $b$ in either order. On derived objects its specified normalization is proper direct image of open extension followed by a resolution comparison. Applying the proper coefficient counit formula of Step 2 and pasting its mates with this sheaf identity gives the coefficient square for that interchange. The proper composition equation from [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] and the open balancing equation then give the coefficient composition square for $h,u$, just as the displayed constituent calculation above did for the coordinate tower. These are comparisons of $B$-adjoints, rather than an equality test after scalar restriction. Transporting this calculation to bounded constructible pro-etale objects uses their etale-origin witnesses and the transported adjunction of Step 3. Thus this total-space etale localization does not require its square over the fixed base to be Cartesian.

source.place: 2.12 and 2.13.2 (ordered products of normalized traces); 3.2.3 (adjoint transposition). The cited affine-space/vector-bundle statements supply the precise local models and global uniqueness.

proof.text:
Now compute the diagonal normalization. Set $W=X\times_YX$, with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\Delta$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion], $\Delta$ is a closed regular section of $p_1$ and $N_\Delta=T_{X/Y}$ has rank $d$. For $R=A,B$ use the section invariants of [def-pur-section-invariant]. The canonical diagonal construction is the chain
$$\alpha_{f,R}:\omega_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_R(p_1,\Delta)\xrightarrow{\delta_R}C_R(\pi_T,0_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X(d)[2d].$$
The first arrow is the inverse of the section identification in [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]; the middle arrow is the uniquely normalized map of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]; the last is zero-section pullback of the normalized vector-bundle identification. This explicitly constructs the canonical identification of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], rather than assuming its coefficient compatibility. All these schemes, the tangent bundle and DNC family are separated finite type over $k$, so they are in the stated domains of the exceptional comparisons. Step 4 proves compatibility of the first arrow, since its dualizing base-change comparison is a counit mate. To compare the middle arrow, use $b$ and pullback to identify $S C_A$ with $C_B$ at both ends. The transported $S\delta_A$ is invertible. In each etale coordinate system from the uniqueness statement, $\delta_A$ is the identity of the standard section invariant. Applying $S$ still gives the identity; the two endpoint coefficient identifications in this standard pair are the same ones. Pullback/scalar-extension commutes by Step 4, and the total-space etale comparisons commute by the final paragraph of Step 6. Thus the transported map satisfies exactly the identity normalization characterizing $\delta_B$; uniqueness in [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] equates them globally. Step 6 proves compatibility of the last arrow, and Step 1 proves the final zero-section twist identification. Pasting the three equations gives
$$\alpha_{f,B}\circ b_{f,A_Y}=S_X(\alpha_{f,A}),$$
where $S_YA_Y=B_Y$ and $S_XT_A=T_B$ are understood. No arbitrary derived maps are being identified by their restrictions: the middle equality uses the cited uniqueness theorem with its exact standard-coordinate normalization.

source.place: 3.2.1--3.2.5, comparison with the blueprint normalization: literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-smooth-purity/sk-thm-smooth-purity/thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object.md, Proof Steps 1--2. Its diagonal/DNC/normal-bundle chain is displayed here and its three coefficient squares are proved, using the statements separately cited.

proof.text:
Write $g_R=\gamma_{f,R_Y}:T_R\to G_{f,R}R_Y$. The definition [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] writes it as twist reassociation, tensor with $\alpha_{f,R}^{-1}$, then the canonical tensor map $\theta$. Step 1 identifies the twist reassociation under $S$, Step 7 identifies $\alpha^{-1}$ (functors preserve inverses), and Step 4 identifies the tensor map by its defining adjoint. For that map the input is the degree-zero coefficient unit; the inverse projection formula in its definition exists by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. Its hypotheses hold since $\omega_{f,R}$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor by [thm-sf-preservation-class], and $R_Y$ has Tor interval $[0,0]$; etale-origin witnesses exist by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Functoriality now gives the precise equality
$$g_B=b_{f,A_Y}\circ S_X(g_A):T_B\longrightarrow G_{f,B}B_Y.$$
Thus the actual normalized purity map, rather than an unspecified purity isomorphism, is the coefficient extension under the canonical exceptional comparison.

source.place: 3.2.3 and 3.2.5: purity is the normalized trace transpose; explicit comparison with the three constituents of the blueprint purity map.

proof.text:
Finally expand the two smooth traces using [def-pur-smooth-trace]: $t_R=\epsilon_{f,R,R_Y}\circ P_{f,R}(g_R)$. Naturality of $c$ at $g_A$ and Step 8 give
$$\begin{aligned}
t_Bc_{T_A}
&=\epsilon_{f,B,B_Y}\,P_{f,B}(b_{f,A_Y})\,P_{f,B}(S_Xg_A)\,c_{T_A}\\
&=\epsilon_{f,B,B_Y}\,P_{f,B}(b_{f,A_Y})\,c_{G_{f,A}A_Y}\,S_Y(P_{f,A}g_A)\\
&=S_Y(\epsilon_{f,A,A_Y})\,S_Y(P_{f,A}g_A)\\
&=S_Y(t_A)=t_A\otimes_A1_B.
\end{aligned}$$
The third line is exactly $(*)$ of Step 3. Every arrow in this calculation is in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$, with the specified coefficient-unit and Tate identifications. The rank-one normalization was fixed by the Kummer class, all further shifts were even, and the DNC comparison was fixed by its identity normalization, so this proves the asserted sign and twist normalization as well as the equality. It also covers $d=0$, $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, and the empty source (all relevant source objects are then zero).

SGA XVIII and the master blueprint were read in the read-only launcher literature cache.
